description:
A repository's event-log size stops deciding whether an issue can be claimed.

## Background

`jit claim acquire` captures the whole event log under a 16 MiB byte budget (`crates/jit/src/commands/claim.rs:191-194`), so a repository whose log exceeds that cannot claim an issue at all. This epic's own benchmark fixture reproduces it at 33 MB: `captured 33519044 bytes but the maximum is 16777216`. The issue-update path sets the same budget at 64 MiB (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2186-2191`), so two mutation paths disagree on a ceiling neither states a reason for.

The claim path reads the whole log to answer a question about its tail. `captured_events` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:695`) parses every line into `Vec<Event>`, and `event_tail_reflects_claim` (`:709`) then scans that result in reverse for the most recent assignment-affecting event for one issue, stopping at the first match.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit claim acquire` succeeds on a repository whose event log exceeds 16 MiB.
- [hard] REQ-02: The claim's convergent behaviour is unchanged: an issue already assigned to the claiming agent with its claim event present emits no event, and an issue assigned without its claim event emits exactly the missing one.
- [hard] REQ-03: The claim and issue-update paths no longer disagree on a byte ceiling; whichever ceiling remains is derived from something, or states in prose why it holds the value it does.
- [hard] REQ-04: A test claims against an event log larger than the previous ceiling and fails if that ceiling returns.

## Notes

Surfaced by this epic's benchmark work (`fe6fa7e5`) rather than by the redo-record design. It is not redo-record work and is excluded from the redo-record subtotal of the REQ-06 line balance.

`c88822a5` later rewrites capture into a single pass and its REQ-03 keeps the event log in the base specification. Whatever shape this task takes must survive that rewrite or be superseded by it.
title: Event-log size stops capping issue claims
